headline: Microsoft surged 5.5% last night while Google slipped 2.5% — a split tech session as oil jumps sharply and the ASX barely moved today.

portfolio.summary: A mixed bag across the portfolio. Microsoft was the standout last night, jumping over 5% to close at $450. Google slid 2.5% — no specific news driving the drop, just a rough session. On the ASX today, CBA pulled back just over 1%, while VGE (emerging markets ETF) was the bright spot, up about 1%. The energy ETF FUEL edged up slightly despite some warning signals about the oil market (more on that below).

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Big jump last night to $450.24 USD — up over $23. No single breaking headline, but corporate earnings have been broadly strong for big tech and MSFT continues to benefit from AI tailwinds across its cloud and productivity businesses.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Slipped $9.79 to $380.34 USD last night with no specific news catalyst. Could be rotation out of Google into Microsoft, or broader sentiment around its AI competition. One to watch.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Up nearly 3% to $224.16 USD last night. GTA 6 buzz continues — developers at Rockstar went public with the company's first union, and speculation about a new GTA 6 trailer dropping in June is building excitement around the stock.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Solid session today, up 1.08% to $92.99. Emerging markets got a lift partly from the slightly stronger Aussie dollar (now 71.8 US cents), which flows through into this ETF's returns.

movers.name: Commonwealth Bank
movers.note: Gave back $1.72 to close at $163.30 today. No specific news — likely some profit-taking after a strong run. CBA remains highly valued by historical standards, so mild pullbacks like this aren't unusual.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: Nudged up 0.71% to $8.52 today. Oil (WTI crude) jumped over 3.5% last night to $90.47 a barrel, which is a clear tailwind for energy companies in this ETF — though Goldman Sachs has warned demand could be approaching a 'destruction' point (where prices get so high people cut back usage).

markets.summary: Last night's US session was calm at the index level — the S&P 500 crept up 0.22% to 7,580 and the NASDAQ added 0.2%. The big action was in oil, which surged 3.56% to $90.47 a barrel. Gold dipped slightly. The Aussie dollar strengthened a touch to 71.8 US cents. The ASX 200 was essentially flat today, down just 0.03%.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Basically flat today — the market trod water ahead of upcoming RBA commentary.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Quiet positive session last night. Markets holding near highs.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Slight gain last night despite Google's drag — Microsoft and others picked up the slack.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Sharp jump last night — oil back above $90, which helps FUEL.AX but raises cost-of-living concerns.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Mild pullback last night as risk appetite returned slightly.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar ticked up slightly — now buying about 71.8 US cents.

politics.summary: A few policy stories bubbling today — gambling reform is drawing fire, Labor is leaning on the Greens to get a tax package through, and the RBA is in focus ahead of upcoming speeches.

stories.title: Labor banks on Greens support to pass tax package after election backflip
stories.why_it_matters: Labor is trying to push through a tax package that it promised before the election, but after apparently changing tack on some details, it now needs the Greens to get it over the line in the Senate. The specifics of what changed aren't fully detailed in the available reporting, but the reliance on the Greens means further negotiation and potential amendments are likely. For investors, any shift in personal tax settings or related economic policy can affect household spending and broader market sentiment.

stories.title: 'Loopholes and deflections': Opponents slam Labor's gambling reform
stories.why_it_matters: Labor's gambling reform legislation is copping heat from opponents who say it's full of loopholes that water down the intent of the reforms. Critics are using words like 'deflections' to describe the government's response to scrutiny. No specific figures are available from the headline alone, but the political fight suggests the reforms may end up weaker than advertised — relevant to anyone watching the gaming and wagering sector.

stories.title: ASX eyes lower open as investors await RBA speeches
stories.why_it_matters: Investors were watching closely for signals from Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) officials speaking this week. The RBA's commentary matters because it shapes expectations about whether interest rates will rise, stay put, or fall — which directly affects mortgage repayments, bank profits (including CBA), and the broader share market. The ASX's flat session today suggests investors are in 'wait and see' mode ahead of those speeches.

ai.summary: The big AI story today is an unusual one — the Pope has waded into the debate, calling for global regulation of AI. Meanwhile, banks are rushing to adopt AI faster than regulators can keep up, and China is tightening investment rules with security implications for tech.

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV issues encyclical calling for AI regulation
stories.source: Let's Data Science / Rocky Mount Telegram
stories.why_it_matters: Pope Leo XIV has issued what's called an encyclical — essentially a formal letter or manifesto sent to Catholics worldwide and beyond — specifically calling for robust regulation of artificial intelligence. It's a significant moment because it signals AI governance has moved from a tech-industry debate to a global moral and political one. When major world institutions like the Catholic Church weigh in, it tends to accelerate pressure on governments to act. For investors in AI-heavy stocks like Google and Microsoft, more regulation could mean compliance costs and limits on certain applications down the track.

stories.title: Banks accelerating AI adoption faster than regulators can handle
stories.why_it_matters: Banks around the world are rolling out AI tools — for fraud detection, customer service, lending decisions — at a pace that's outrunning the ability of regulators to write the rules. This creates a risk: if something goes wrong (biased lending decisions, privacy breaches), banks could face big fines or forced changes later. For CBA holders, it's worth knowing that Australian banks are in the same race, and regulatory catch-up is coming. The upside is that AI is genuinely cutting costs and improving efficiency for banks right now.

stories.title: China tightens outbound investment rules with eye on security
stories.why_it_matters: China is tightening rules around Chinese companies or investors putting money overseas, with national security as the stated reason. This matters for your VGE emerging markets ETF, which has significant exposure to Chinese companies. Tighter capital controls can dampen the ability of Chinese firms to grow internationally and may signal a more inward-looking policy stance — which markets historically don't love. Worth keeping an eye on how this develops over the coming weeks.

sport.summary: Ben Cousins' MND diagnosis has shocked Australian sport, the Broncos are under pressure heading into Round 14, and the NRL's newest star put on a show in Round 13. Plus, there's transfer news with the Tigers closing in on a halves replacement.

stories.title: Ben Cousins diagnosed with MND — Aussie sport in mourning
stories.why_it_matters: Former West Coast Eagles captain and 2005 Brownlow Medallist Ben Cousins has been diagnosed with Motor Neurone Disease (MND) — a devastating, degenerative condition that affects the nerves controlling movement, with no cure. Cousins, who had a very public battle with drug addiction after his playing days, had been living a relatively private life in recent years. The AFL world has rallied around his family with an outpouring of support. An incredibly sad story for one of the most talented and troubled figures in Australian sport.

stories.title: Broncos' bad run continues — Haas calls out 'BS' as Maguire urges caution
stories.why_it_matters: Payne Haas has publicly vented frustration at what he called 'BS' surrounding the Broncos, as the club's poor form continues to draw scrutiny. Coach Jason Maguire is urging the side not to rely on another miracle comeback and to fix their problems properly. With the Broncos hosting the Titans at Suncorp Stadium on Saturday night in Round 14, there's plenty of pressure on — and for Gold Coast fans, the Titans will be looking to capitalise.

stories.title: Tigers close in on Luai replacement from Dolphins
stories.why_it_matters: Wests Tigers are reportedly close to signing a halfback from the Dolphins to replace Jarome Luai, who departed the club. The player's name wasn't confirmed in the headline, but it signals the Tigers are actively rebuilding their halves combination. With the Tigers hosting the Panthers at CommBank Stadium on Sunday in Round 14, the timing of this news adds some transfer drama to the lead-up.

stories.title: GTA 6 developers form Rockstar Games' first-ever union
stories.why_it_matters: Developers working on GTA 6 at Rockstar Games have gone public as the studio's first-ever union. This is a landmark moment for the games industry — Rockstar is one of the biggest and most profitable studios in the world. For Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) shareholders, unionisation could mean higher labour costs and potentially slower development timelines, though it may also improve retention of key talent. GTA 6 is the most anticipated game release in years and its success is critical to Take-Two's share price outlook.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Hold after big jump — don't chase it
watch_today.detail: Microsoft surged 5.45% last night to $450.24 — a great result, but after a move that big it's worth resisting the urge to add more at the top. No single catalyst has been confirmed, and the stock may consolidate in the near term. Sit tight and enjoy the gain.

watch_today.title: GOOGL: Watch for a bounce or further weakness
watch_today.detail: Google dropped 2.5% last night to $380.34 with no clear news driver. Could be rotation from Google into Microsoft or Apple, or nerves about AI competition. No reason to sell — but keep an eye on it this week. If it keeps sliding without a news reason, it might be worth revisiting your position.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 union news — mild risk to watch
watch_today.detail: Rockstar developers have formed the studio's first union. Short-term, this doesn't change the GTA 6 release outlook — but if it leads to industrial action or delays, Take-Two's most important product could be impacted. Stock is up 2.9% anyway on GTA hype. Hold for now, watch for any escalation.

watch_today.title: Oil above $90 — FUEL.AX gets a tailwind, but Goldman warns of demand risk
watch_today.detail: WTI crude oil jumped 3.56% last night to $90.47 — that's good for your energy ETF in the short run. But Goldman Sachs has flagged that energy markets may be entering a 'demand destruction' phase, meaning prices could be getting high enough that consumers and businesses start cutting back, which would eventually drag oil back down. Fine to hold, but be aware this strength may not last.

watch_today.title: RBA speeches this week — watch for interest rate signals
watch_today.detail: Reserve Bank of Australia officials are speaking this week, and markets are listening closely. Any hint that rates are staying higher for longer could put pressure on the ASX — particularly rate-sensitive stocks like CBA. Keep an eye on headlines Wednesday–Friday.
